topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing plays a critical role in shaping coverage patterns and managing grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links. A balance between narrower and wider element spacing is essential to achieve high directivity and robust grating lobe suppression. By carefully tuning the element spacing, engineers can optimize the array factor to maximize system performance and minimize interference. In particular, a hybrid approach combining narrower and wider spacing within the array can provide a balanced solution, while adaptive algorithms can further optimize the array factor in real-time.
